newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MAY 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MAY 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Public servants taking their retirement before December 31, 1996 will receive increases of above 8.0 percent and up to 16 percent, according to a law readjusting pensions to the new wage scale, presented by Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis.
--Technical problems with the electronic trading system at the Athens Stock Exchange could not deal with the high demand to buy Xiosbank shares yesterday and forced the closure of the session.
--Nine hundred representatives from the shipping community and, specifically, from the petroleum transport field, began their second Intertanko conference in Athens yesterday.

--There's chaos at Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, with reports that there are not enough cabin crews to staff planned flights. The confusion caused delays and queues at the weekend and cancellation of flights to Moscow and other European destinations.
IMERISIA

--The cancellation of the first trading session after the Athens bourse set a new record last week has called the credibility of the bourse into question. Today, the bourse authorities are considered setting limits on the trading of XiosBank shares to prevent the technical system overloading for a second day.

--Sources say the first public organisations and enterprises to be merged or abolished as part of plans to quickly cut back on public spending will be OPE, the foreign trade board, and ELKEPA, the productivity and training centre. Both will be merged with other organisations.
KERDOS
--There are reports that dissatisfied customers at an Athens bank will seek legal action over alleged embezzlement of up to 200 million drachmas.
--The government is not planning to do away with the Christmas or Easter bonus for waged workers, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis.
--The administrative board of OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, will discuss procurements contracts worth 160 billion drachmas at its meeting today with the final decisions expected tomorrow.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--The overwhelming demand at the bourse yesterday for Xiosbank shares - which saw the price soar by 103 percent before technical problems stopped trading - will be the focus of the Capital Market Commission's this morning to examine whether to put a limit of 20 percent on the movement of newly-listed shares.
--Banks are apparently bidding for the lion's share of OTE's second share offer next month, according to reports.
--The European Investment Bank is expected to issue a 200 billion drachma bond loan to Greece for financing of works in the Community Support Framework.
EXPRESS
--Procedural issues will be the focus of talks today at the first real 'social dialogue' meeting between government, unions and employers on changes to the job market.

--Construction activity was on a stable upward course in the period January-February, according to statistics. Activity was up 8.9 percent in comparison to the same period last year. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
